notes:
Account background: mid-market/enterprise financial tech platform (loan origination + fraud analytics). Heavy real-time constraints for customer-facing search and chat; latency sensitivity for pre-approval flows. They run sensitive PII and require VPC/private control plane, KMS, strict retention and audit logs.

Why Redwood eval: they want a single runtime for hosted-like developer ergonomics but with dedicated predictable throughput and certified SLA (99.9% p95 SLA target). Concerned about cold-starts and queueing behavior when batch traffic spikes at 10:30am/2:00pm business peaks.

POC scope: dedicated reserved cluster (8x A10G equiv GPUs initially) with autoscaling policy review, warm-pool strategy, and throughput guarantees under real traffic replay. Focus metrics: p50/p95 token latency, sustained QPS, end-to-end request latency for chat reranking pipeline (goal p95 < 350ms for 20 QPS per tenant). Cost guardrails to stay within projected ARR.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call w/ AE (Ethan) + SE (Priya). Collected traffic profile CSV + sample prompts. Action: SE to run perf estimate.
- 2026-02-02: Architecture workshop (drive deck shared). Discussed VPC peering and KMS. Legal requested SLA redline template.
- 2026-02-18: Fireflies transcript: product owner: "We need guaranteed tail latency or regulator fines pile up." Confirmed they will replay 72 hours of production traffic for POC.
- 2026-02-25: SE lab run: baseline with 4x GPUs shows p95 spike to ~820ms under burst. Suggested warm-pool of kept-hot worker count to reduce cold-start.
- 2026-03-03: Internal Redwood pricing review + draft SOW v1 sent (drive link).
- 2026-03-05: Follow-up call; customer asks for concrete autoscaling policy examples and warm pool sizing formulas.

Technical notes / customer constraints: 
- Target throughput: steady 25 QPS across 3 tenants, burst to 100 QPS for 30s windows.
- Latency SLO targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for chat-generation (decoder-only 13B-ish models); endpoints for reranking must stay p95 < 200ms.
- Prefers open LLMs (13B quantized variants) with option to pin to older faster checkpoints. Multi-model routing: primary = gptx-13b-q8, fallback = gptx-7b-q4 for cost fallthrough.
- KV cache warmup: significant warm-up time when new model shards spin up; recommended prefetch policy for top-10 prefixes.
- Batching: want aggressive batching during steady-state but strict single-request low-latency path for user-facing flows.
- Warm pools: customer leaning to a 30% warm-pool (2 kept-hot GPUs) for initial cluster to cut cold start tail by ~60-70%. SE estimates warm-pool cost delta ~+15% ARR vs fully reactive autoscale.

Autoscaling discussion items surfaced: 
- Scale-up policy options: immediate scale on queue depth vs thresholded by sustained CPU/GPU utilization over 5s window. Customer prefers queue-length trigger to protect latency but wants max ramp rate to avoid overshoot.
- Scale-down policy: aggressive decay leads to oscillation during work bursts. Recommended cool-down of 120s with batch-aware decisioning (drain queued batches before scale-in).
- Warm pool sizing: formula proposed by SE: warm_pool_gpus = ceil(peak_burst_tokens_per_sec / gpu_token_throughput) * safety_factor (1.2) clipped to min 1. Customer asked for deterministic bound to include in SLA (warm pool hit rate target 95%).
- Queueing behavior: need visibility into per-route queue depth, per-tenant fairness queues, and estimated wait time. Discussed soft-priority for latency-sensitive routes and preemption of batch jobs.

SLA & contract negotiation points: 
- Customer wants p95 latency-backed SLA for reserved cluster (will accept credits for breaches). Legal submitted redline asking for explicit warm-pool inclusion and defined upgrade windows (30 minutes for scale to X capacity). Redwood to propose measurable metrics and runbooks.
- Request to include autoscale-proof test cases in acceptance criteria: replayed traffic demonstrating <350ms p95 over 30-minute ramp tests.

Open action items: 
- SE (Priya) to provide warm-pool sizing spreadsheet and simulated cost delta by 2026-03-10 (IN PROGRESS).
- AE (Ethan) to coordinate Legal <> Sales on SLA redline and propose compromise language by 2026-03-12.
- Infra team to prepare a replay harness and schedule POC window (customer provided 72h sample) for week of 2026-03-22.
- Customer to share final network diagram and approved PKI for VPC peering (blocker for on-prem path).

Customer quote (paraphrased): "We can trade a bit of cost for guaranteed tail behavior — if you can show consistent p95 under our replay we'll move to committed capacity."

Next-step (short): send warm-pool sizing + autoscale policy examples, finalize SOW redline, schedule replay POC.
